llm.summary: This skill openly automates social posting, but it needs careful review because it can publish to multiple public accounts from a short command and handles account credentials unsafely.

dimensions.detail: The skill requires social-platform and R2 credentials, uploads generated media to external services, and launches Chromium with --no-sandbox for rendering; these are not hidden, but they are broad for an agent skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The README instructs users to run an unpinned npx install command, and the Python dependencies are listed without versions or integrity controls.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The documented command "Post now" immediately posts to all configured platforms, with no clear required preview, per-platform scoping, or confirmation gate in the skill instructions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: YouTube OAuth credentials are stored in a predictable project-root token file and loaded with pickle before JSON fallback, creating avoidable credential and local code-execution risk if the token file is tampered with.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The posting, commenting, video generation, and R2 upload behavior matches the stated social automation purpose, but it is high-impact because it can publish public content across X, Instagram, YouTube, and Meta accounts.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving the skill real posting rights on the connected accounts. Use test accounts first, limit API scopes, review generated content before publishing, avoid the generic all-platform trigger, pin installer and dependency versions, store YouTube tokens outside the project with restrictive permissions, and run video rendering in an isolated environment without production credentials.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: The Meta network request sends a configured page token to the Meta Graph API for posting; this is expected API authentication, not artifact-backed unrelated exfiltration.
[PE3] expected: The access-token and client-secret references are expected for social-platform integrations, but users should treat them as sensitive production account authority.
[SQP-2] expected: Automatic public posting is the advertised purpose, but the artifacts do not provide a prominent safety warning or approval gate for account-modifying actions.
[SQP-1] unexpected: The short trigger "Post now" is under-scoped for a multi-platform publish action and supports the Review verdict.
[RP1] unexpected: The unpinned npx install command is not needed for the skill's purpose and creates mutable installer risk.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The security note that the content database is never uploaded is incomplete: the raw CSV may stay local, but CSV-derived text and media are published externally.
[SQP-3] expected: The locale-specific UPSC/Hinglish content appears to be a customization and quality issue, not a standalone security basis for escalation.
[E5] expected: The Cloudflare R2 upload is disclosed and purpose-aligned for Instagram reel hosting, though users must control the bucket and avoid sensitive content.
[AST10] unexpected: Loading the YouTube token file with pickle is a real unsafe deserialization concern and is not necessary for the posting workflow.
[T09] unexpected: The static findings for pickle credential loading, plaintext project-root token persistence, and default Chromium --no-sandbox are supported by the inspected code.
[T08] unexpected: The static finding about the unpinned remote npm installer is supported by the README install command.
